title: Hard Drive Reliability Wars: New Study Crowns HGST & WD Over Seagate & Toshiba
summary: A comprehensive, peer-reviewed IEEE study analyzed data from over 443,000 hard drives in Backblaze data centers, spanning from 2013 to Q2 2025. The research revealed that HGST and Western Digital drives consistently exhibit lower failure rates compared to their counterparts from Seagate and Toshiba, even after accounting for critical factors like age and capacity.
content:
In the never-ending quest for digital peace of mind, the reliability of our hard drives remains a paramount concern. Now, a substantial new peer-reviewed study sheds crucial light on which brands stand the test of time, delivering a decisive verdict that will likely influence countless purchasing decisions for consumers and enterprises alike.

The research, published by the IEEE and authored by Christoph Siemroth of the University of Essex and Yeomyung Park of Sungkyunkwan University, delves deep into the performance metrics of hundreds of thousands of drives. They meticulously analyzed data from a colossal fleet of 443,156 hard drives operating within Backblaze's data centers. This extensive dataset spans an impressive period, from 2013 right through to the second quarter of 2025, offering an unprecedented look at long-term drive endurance.

The bottom line is clear: HGST and Western Digital drives emerged as the champions of dependability. The study concluded that these brands consistently exhibited notably lower failure rates when stacked against their competitors, Seagate and Toshiba. Crucially, this finding holds true even after the researchers meticulously accounted for significant variables such as the drives' age and their storage capacity, factors that can often skew reliability metrics.

This isn't just academic curiosity; it's a vital piece of information for anyone entrusting their precious data to spinning platters. Whether you're a home user building a robust backup system or an IT professional managing a vast array of servers, understanding these differences can translate directly into fewer data loss incidents and reduced operational headaches. While all hard drives will eventually fail, this study offers compelling evidence that some manufacturers are simply building more resilient hardware from the outset.
keyTakeaways: A major IEEE study found HGST and Western Digital hard drives to be significantly more reliable than Seagate and Toshiba models.
The research analyzed data from over 443,000 drives in Backblaze's data centers, controlling for age and capacity.
These findings offer crucial guidance for consumers and businesses prioritizing data integrity and drive longevity.
author: Skye Jacobs
